Contents
Exide Industries 
Limited presents its 
third Integrated Annual 
Report for the financial 
year 2025–26, marking 
continued progress in 
integrated reporting 
and long-term value 
creation. 
The Report outlines the Company’s 
strategic direction, operational 
performance and key initiatives across 
environmental, social and governance 
(ESG) dimensions. By aligning with 
globally recognised reporting standards, 
the report provides a comprehensive 
view of how Exide continues to drive 
sustainable growth, responsible 
business practices and stakeholder 
value in an evolving business 
environment.
Reporting period and boundary
This Report presents the financial 
and non-financial performance for the 
period 1st April 2025 to 31st March 2026. 
The report has been prepared on a 
standalone basis.
Reporting Framework
This Report has been prepared in 
alignment with the criteria set by the 
Global Sustainability Standards Board 
(GSSB) under the GRI Standards. It is 
guided by the principles of the National 
Voluntary Guidelines and aligned 
with the United Nations Sustainable 
Development Goals (SDGs).
Materiality Approach
Our materiality approach is grounded 
in a Double Materiality Assessment 
(DMA), conducted in FY 2025-26, 
evaluating sustainability topics through 
two lenses - their impact on people 
and planet (impact materiality) and 
their effect on business value (financial 
materiality). The assessment is aligned 
with GRI Standards and informed by 
structured stakeholder engagement, 
ensuring that the topics most significant 
to our business and stakeholders are 
identified, prioritised, and integrated into 
our sustainability strategy.
Forward-Looking Statements
Certain statements contained in this 
Report are forward-looking in nature. 
These include references to market 
scenarios, business dynamics, company 
strategy and future prospects, and 
exclude historical facts and past financial 
performance, which are not forward-
looking in nature. Such statements 
involve both identified and unidentified 
risks and uncertainties that could cause 
actual results to differ materially from 
those expressed or implied.

About

Movement in India is constant. It shows up in 
the morning start of a two-wheeler, the long 
haul of a truck, the everyday drive of a family 
car, and in the dependable running of homes, 
offices, telecom networks, railways and essential 
infrastructure. Behind each of these moments is 
a simple expectation that 
“Moving India.
Then, Now and 
Tomorrow”
power must remain 
dependable.
In India, where internal combustion engine vehicles still 
account for nearly 90% of the automotive market, demand 
continues to be driven by proven, accessible and dependable 
solutions. At Exide, we remain closely aligned with market 
realities, customer needs and evolving demand across 
two-wheelers, four-wheelers and Original Equipment 
Manufacturers (OEMs), with reliability at the core. 
From last-mile mobility and home backup to industrial 
infrastructure and solar applications, Exide’s presence 
reflects the breadth and depth of its portfolio. We are also 
strengthening digital engagement to connect faster and more 
directly with customers while strengthening our leadership 
anchored in trust, reach and scale.
An Industry Built to Endure
New developments and reliable systems over time drive 
India’s growth. The lead acid battery industry, a mature,  
well-established sector, is one of the most circular industries. 
Invented as far back as 1859, the lead-acid battery has 
evolved over decades to support vehicles, industries and 
critical applications with dependable performance. Demand 
here is driven more by continuity than by cycles of disruption.
As automotive OEMs continue to invest in internal 
combustion engine platforms, the relevance of lead-acid 
batteries remains intact. More importantly, with a vast 
installed base of vehicles already on the road, replacement 
demand continues to anchor the industry, creating a stable 
revenue stream.
Across nearly eight decades and five 
continents, Exide has been the silent 
force behind supporting millions of users 
simultaneously. We take pride in our 
heritage as the perennial market leader in 
power storage. From our first day to the 
present, our mission remains unchanged 
to provide reliable energy solutions 
catering to multiple applications.
Where Reliability Drives Demand
In this environment, consistency matters more than novelty. 
Replacement remains at the core of the business, driven by 
everyday needs where performance cannot falter. Whether it is 
a two-wheeler navigating city streets or a commercial vehicle 
powering long-distance logistics or powering millions of homes 
or supporting critical infrastructure growth, dependable energy 
is still the need of the hour.
Our strength lies in understanding this reality. Over the 
years, we have built a strong presence, both in the OEM 
business and in the replacement market, supported by 
deep distribution, reliable products, strong brand recall 
and long-standing customer trust. This ability to deliver, 
repeatedly and reliably, has defined our leadership.
Evolving with the Shift
The broader energy landscape is gradually evolving with 
technologies such as Li-ion across emerging applications. 
However, this transition is expected to be gradual, shaped 
by infrastructure readiness, cost dynamics and real-world 
usage patterns.
Through our strategic investment in Exide Energy Solutions 
Limited (EESL), Exide is building capabilities to support 
India’s emerging energy needs. As India moves toward 
electrification and greater grid resilience, Exide is taking 
a proactive and measured approach. While continuing to 
strengthen its leadership in the core lead-acid business, the 
Company is expanding its Li-ion capabilities as a natural 
extension of its portfolio. This ensures readiness while 
staying aligned with the current market scenario.
In Step with India’s Progress
India’s journey forward will be defined by both continuity 
and change. Systems that have proven their strength will 
continue to power the present, even as new technologies 
shape the future.
We remain closely aligned with this 
journey, supporting what drives India 
today while preparing thoughtfully for 
what will drive it tomorrow. Because true 
progress is not about choosing between 
the present and the future but about 
powering both seamlessly. 

Energy today is being 
redefined in real time. 
What once depended 
primarily on scale is now 
increasingly shaped by 
intelligence, efficiency, 
sustainability and 
the ability to perform 
reliably across a far more 
interconnected world.
As industries evolve and

At Exide, we see ourselves as an

Supporting continuity where

change where the future is being

Resilience 
Strength that Endures
Reliable power remains fundamental to 
the functioning of modern economies, 
supporting mobility, infrastructure, 
industry and essential services that 
depend on uninterrupted performance. 
From powering vehicles to supporting 
critical infrastructure across railways, 
power, defence and industrial 
applications, our solutions remain 
integral to everyday movement and 
economic continuity. 
Built on scale, deep market 
understanding and decades of 
consistent performance, we have 
earned enduring trust across 
sectors where reliability, quality and 
dependable delivery are essential.
Ready  
Future Already  
in Motion
Preparing for the future requires 
strengthening the businesses that sustain 
the present while building capabilities for 
the energy systems of tomorrow.
At Exide, our focus remains anchored 
around two strategic priorities: 
Strengthening our core lead-acid 
business and scaling our new energy 
platform centred on lithium-ion 
technologies. Within lead-acid, we 
continue to lead the industry through 
technology-led products, strong 
manufacturing capabilities, extensive 
service reach and diversified application 
presence across automotive, industrial, 
data centre, solar, infrastructure, power 
and project segments.
At the same time, we are steadily 
advancing our lithium-ion cell 
manufacturing plans through a phased 
capacity build-out of up to 12 GWh. 
This positions us to participate in 
emerging growth opportunities across 
electric mobility and energy storage. 
Supported by strategic global 
collaborations, we continue to 
strengthen competitiveness, expand 
international access and create a more 
diversified and future-ready business 
portfolio aligned with evolving energy 
transition opportunities. 
Responsible 
Discipline Behind  
Sustainable Progress
Powering Circular Progress
Our sustainability approach is 
embedded in circularity. Nearly 79% of 
our lead and lead alloy requirements 
are met through recycled sources, 
supported by our wholly owned 
subsidiary and closed-loop system 
material recovery system. This vertical 
integration model strengthens resource 
security while supporting compliance 
with extended producer responsibility 
under battery waste, e-waste and 
plastic waste management regulations.
Advancing Resource 
Responsibility
Renewables now contribute over 
24% of our electricity mix, while 
water stewardship, including ZLD 
systems and both within-fence and 
outside-fence rainwater collection and 
harvesting interventions, continues to 
strengthen our progress towards water 
neutrality. In last-mile logistics, the 0–50 
km EV fleet has surpassed the 2030 
target, achieving 26% deployment 
against a 20% goal.

Chairman’s Message
Dear Shareholders,
FY 2025-26 unfolded 
against a backdrop 
of heightened global 
uncertainty. For Exide, it 
was a year of calculated 
progress—marked by 
steady performance in the 
core business, continued 
institution building, and 
measured investments for 
the future. As we reflect 
on the year, we believe 
the Company’s enduring 
relevance lies not only in the 
products it manufactures 
today, but in its ability to 
adapt to change while 
remaining anchored to long 
term value creation.
Global and Industry context
The global macro environment in 
FY 2025-26 remained unsettled with 
varied degrees of uncertainties. The 
global economy grew by 3.4% in 2025, 
although the quality of growth remained 
uneven across regions. Emerging 
markets and developing economies 
grew by 4.4%, while advanced 
economies registered growth of 1.9%, 
reflecting divergent economic cycles.
Trade disputes, geopolitical shifts and 
supply-chain disruptions kept industrial 
activity subdued across markets. 
Elevated commodity prices and adverse 
currency movements coupled with 
capital outflows, turned more aggressive 
as policymakers balanced growth, 
inflation and financial stability. 
In such an environment, businesses 
with strong balance sheets, operational 
discipline, and prudent capital allocation 
frameworks were better positioned to 
navigate uncertainty.
Amid these global headwinds, India 
remained a relative bright spot, with 
FY 2025-26 GDP growth estimated at 
6.6%, supported by strong domestic 
consumption, sustained public capital 
expenditure and an improving rural 
economy.
Continued investments in infrastructure, 
railways, data centres, renewable energy 
and electric mobility are expected 
to create a broad-based demand 
environment over the medium term, 
reinforcing the long-term relevance of 
the sectors that Exide serves.
Core Business Strength and 
Portfolio Resilience
Exide’s lead acid battery business 
continues to be a diversified and cash-
generative platform, serving a wide 
range of applications across automotive 
replacement and Original Equipment 
Manufacturers (OEMs), home power, 
industrial UPS, railways, traction, solar, 
infrastructure, and defence. This breadth 
remains a key strength, reducing 
exposure to any single end market and 
supporting resilience across cycles.
From a Board perspective, the 
core business is not viewed as a 
legacy asset. The priority remains to 
continuously improve product relevance, 
manufacturing efficiency, distribution 
reach, service quality, and market 
leadership, even as the Company 
selectively builds capabilities for 
emerging energy applications.
Capital Allocation and 
Technology Transition
The battery industry is clearly moving 
through a technology transition, 
although the pace of change differs 
by application. Lead acid batteries 
Responsible and Sustainable 
Growth
The Board continues to emphasise that 
Exide’s long-term success is rooted not 
only in its assets and technologies but also 
in its people and communities. During the 
year, our Company sustained its focus on 
leadership development, organisational 
capability, safety, and inclusion, including 
over 95,000 hours of EHS training.
Corporate social responsibility remains 
an integral part of Exide’s operating 
philosophy. Through its five CSR pillars-
Akshar, Aarogya, Kaushal, Paryavaran, 
and Saksham, our Company supported 
education, healthcare, livelihoods, 
environmental stewardship, and women’s 
empowerment across multiple states.
Strong partnerships with community 
organisations and active employee 
participation continue to ensure that 
these initiatives deliver meaningful 
and locally relevant outcomes. During 
the year, these initiatives reached 
communities across 26 districts and 10 
states, positively impacting 4 Lakh+ 
individuals, with approximately 80% of 
them drawn from vulnerable groups.
Aligned with our broader societal 
role, we continued in our journey of 
strengthening our ESG performance, 
shaped by a systemic approach to 
circularity and resource optimization. 
Close to 79% of our total lead and 
lead-alloys requirements were met 
through recycled inputs. We source 
~50% of total lead requirement through 
recycled lead procurement from our 
subsidiary, Chloride Metals Limited, 
epitomising our belief in circularity 
in operations and lowering our 
environmental impact. During the year, 
Exide also received a Bronze EcoVadis 
sustainability rating, ranking in the top 
14% of the ‘Manufacture of Batteries & 
Accumulators’ industry globally, with a 
score of 67/100.
Looking Ahead
As we enter FY 2026-27, opportunities 
across Exide’s core markets remain 
constructive, even as global volatility 
persists. Geopolitical developments, 
commodity prices, currency movements, 
and ongoing technology shifts will 
require continued vigilance and 
disciplined execution.
The Board remains focused on 
strengthening the cash-generating core 
business, improving capital productivity, 
progressing future-ready investments 
with rigour, maintaining strong 
governance standards, and preserving 
balance sheet strength. We believe 
Exide is well positioned to participate 
meaningfully in India’s growth and the 
evolving energy storage landscape, 
supported by its brand strength, 
distribution reach, manufacturing depth, 
service infrastructure, and prudent 
approach to capital allocation.
Gratitude
On behalf of the Board, I extend our 
sincere gratitude to our shareholders 
for their continued trust and confidence. 
I also convey my appreciation to our 
employees, customers, channel partners, 
and all stakeholders for their invaluable 
contributions to Exide’s journey. We are 
confident that Exide is well-positioned to 
navigate the evolving energy landscape 
and deliver sustained value creation. We 
look forward to your continued support as 
we advance on this exciting journey.
Regards,
Sridhar Gorthi

Financial Discipline and 
Balance Sheet Strength
During FY26, the Company delivered 
standalone revenue of H17,269 crore with 
EBITDA and PBT of H1,943 crore and 
H1,500 crore respectively. Importantly, 
Exide remained debt-free, supported 
by strong liquidity and consistent cash 
generation, enabling the Company to 
fund strategic investments through 
internal accruals.
The Board views this financial resilience 
as a critical strength—particularly in a 
period of macroeconomic volatility and 
technological evolution. It provides Exide 
with the flexibility to invest for the future 
while maintaining balance sheet strength 
and protecting shareholder returns.

MD and CEO’s Message
Dear Shareholders,
FY 2025-26 was a year 
of disciplined execution 
for Exide, delivered in 
a complex operating 
environment marked by 
geopolitical uncertainty, 
commodity and currency 
volatility, technology shifts 
in battery applications, 
and uneven demand 
conditions. Despite these 
challenges, India sustained 
its position as one of the 
fastest-growing major 
economies, creating 
opportunities across 
automotive, replacement, 
industrial, infrastructure, and 
energy storage markets. 
Our priorities during the 
year were clear - deliver 
steady performance in 
core businesses, sharpen 
execution, and continue 
building capabilities for 
long-term growth.
The domestic environment remained 
broadly supportive, driven by 
infrastructure spending, improving rural 
demand, and Goods and Services 
Tax (GST) reforms. At the same time, 
global disruptions and input cost 
volatility continued to pose challenges. 
We responded with agile pricing, 
disciplined inventory management, 
and sharper market execution, while 
maintaining focus on technology, 
product development, and capacity 
enhancement.
Mid-year GST rationalisation and 
easing inflation supported automotive 
and consumer demand, though 
international markets remained volatile 
and technology migration in segments 
such as telecom required portfolio 
recalibration.
Synergy in Motion
Business performance in FY 2025-26 
was resilient, though differentiated.

supported by improving replacement 
cycles and increasing preference for 
organised and trusted brands. Original 
Equipment Manufacturers (OEM) 
demand strengthened alongside higher 
vehicle production, driven by new model 
launches and improved affordability. 
Industrial businesses- covering Industrial 
UPS (I-UPS), railways, traction, and 
infrastructure- benefited from India’s 
sustained capital investment cycle. 
Home inverters, batteries, and solar 
businesses delivered steady growth. 
The telecom segment continued to 
face structural headwinds due to the 
transition toward lithium ion technology. 
International operations remained 
affected by geopolitical uncertainty, 
although continued market expansion 
and channel development strengthened 
the growth prospects.

Advanced Driver Assistance System 
(ADAS) and start-stop vehicles, high-
durability batteries for mining and 
heavy-duty applications, improved EV 
auxiliary batteries, and Valve Regulated 
Lead Acid (VRLA) solutions aligned with 
evolving data centre and renewable 
energy requirements.
We also continued to strengthen go-to-
market and service capabilities through 
digital initiatives, improving data visibility, 
turnaround times, and field productivity, 
while enhancing channel engagement 
and capability building.
Future Ready
Our lithium ion battery business 
progressed steadily, with internal 
validation, commissioning, and plant 
readiness advancing across cylindrical 
and prismatic lines. The focus remains 
on disciplined ramp-up, quality, and

cumulative equity investment in this 
business to H4,802 crore.

Sustainability continues to be integrated 
into our operating philosophy. During 
the year, we added 14 MWp of solar 
open access capacity, taking total solar 
capacity to 95.3 MWp, complemented 
by 11.7 MW of wind capacity. Water 
efficiency improvements enhanced 
recovery rates from ~52% to ~80%. 
Our S&P Global Corporate Sustainability 
Assessment score improved by 
approximately 50% YoY, placing Exide 
among the top 5% of global auto 
components companies.
The Road Ahead 
Looking ahead to FY 2026-27, we 
remain constructive but watchful. 
Geopolitical tensions, particularly in West 
Asia, could drive volatility in fuel and raw 
material prices. Inflationary pressures 
on the supply side and higher interest 
rates may temper demand. However, 
opportunities remain robust across 
automotive replacement and OEMs, 
solar, railways, industrial UPS, traction, 
and infrastructure-linked segments.
Our strategic priorities remain 
unchanged- strengthen the lead acid 
franchise, deepen product offerings,  
and build scalable capabilities in lithium-
ion and advanced energy storage 
solutions. We will continue to focus 
on innovation, customer relevance, 
distribution depth, service quality, and 
capital discipline to deliver sustainable 
long-term value to our investors.

India remained one of the fastest-
growing major economies globally 
during the year, supported by structural 
reforms and resilient domestic demand. 
In FY 2025-262, economic growth was 
aided by improving investor sentiment, 
relatively accommodative financial 
conditions and benign inflation. The 
government’s continued emphasis on 
infrastructure creation was reflected in 
the capital expenditure allocation of  
H10.96 lakh crore for FY 2025-26.
Manufacturing activity also remained 
encouraging through most of the 
year. The Manufacturing Purchasing 
Managers’ Index (PMI) stayed strong, 
supported by healthy order inflows and 
productivity gains. The Index of Industrial 
Production for the manufacturing sector 
also improved as the year progressed, 
aided in part by steady growth in 
automotive manufacturing. 
On the demand side, rural consumption 
remained stable, while urban demand 
exhibited signs of recovery, aided by 
GST rationalisation and favourable 
monetary conditions. CPI inflation 
moderated during the year, largely driven 
by lower food prices.
In response to evolving global risks, 
the RBI maintained a calibrated stance 
to balance growth and inflation. 
However, elevated crude oil prices, 
capital outflows and inflation concerns 
continued to drive currency volatility, 
placing the rupee under near-term 
pressure. The depreciation of the INR 
against the US dollar is also likely to 
influence import costs and overall input 
cost dynamics across the industry. 
LME lead prices remained relatively 
soft on average, though intermittent 
spikes continued to exert cost pressure. 
Nevertheless, the impact of such 
volatility can be managed through 
disciplined inventory planning and timely 
price revisions.
Further, the ongoing West Asia conflict 
has heightened concerns around 
fuel availability and price volatility, 
accelerating interest in electric mobility 
across key segments. This shift is further 
supported by strong policy momentum, 
with both central and state governments 
actively evaluating measures to promote 
EV adoption. Regulatory developments, 
including evolving fuel efficiency norms, 
are expected to increase the share 
of electric vehicles across the OEM 
portfolio. For instance, Delhi’s draft EV 
Policy 2026–2030 proposes that, from 
1st April 2028, only electric 2-wheelers 
will be permitted for new registration in 
the NCT of Delhi, signalling the policy 
direction towards faster EV adoption.

Exide has, over seven decades, 
cultivated a distinguished reputation 
as one of India’s foremost storage 
battery manufacturers. The Company’s 
sustained emphasis on innovation, 
complemented by global technology 
alliances and an expansive geographic 
footprint, has enabled it to establish 
leadership across both automotive and 
industrial lead-acid batteries. Its portfolio 
spans conventional flooded batteries 
as well as advanced Valve-Regulated 
Lead-Acid (VRLA) batteries, catering to 
a wide spectrum of applications. This 
depth, supported by a dominant market 
position and a growing presence in key 
export markets, continues to strengthen 
its competitive standing. In FY 2025-26, 
the Company made significant strides 
to align its quality product offerings 
and leverage its nationwide distribution 
network with the evolving energy 
requirements. This was supported by 
the steady expansion of the vehicle 
base, rising energy intensity driven by 
advanced automotive electronics and 
the growing scale of commercial fleets 
powering inter-city logistics, intra-city 
distribution and last-mile delivery. 
recycling ecosystem through its 
wholly-owned subsidiary, Chloride 
Metals Limited, strengthening resource 
efficiency and supply security.
Despite the emergence of alternative 
chemistries, lead-acid batteries continue 
to retain relevance across a wide range 
of applications due to their safety profile, 
cost competitiveness and proven 
performance. Continued investments 
by OEMs in internal combustion engine 
platforms are expected to support 
steady replacement and OEM-linked 
demand. While lithium-ion is gaining 
traction in select applications, it is better 
viewed as an additional technology 
stream rather than a full substitute 
across the broader battery landscape.
FY 2025-26 was a two-phase year: 
Demand conditions remained relatively 
subdued during April to September, 
reflecting cautious consumer spending 
and uncertainty ahead of GST 2.0. 
However, momentum improved 
meaningfully from October to March, 
supported by a post-GST 2.0 demand 
recovery and a visible pickup in 
consumer purchases.
During the financial year, passenger 
vehicle retail sales reached 47.05 Lakh 
units, representing a 13% YoY growth. 
The favourable demand environment 
also supported other sub-segments 
of the automotive sector. 2-wheeler 
retail sales also rose to 21.42 million 
units, registering a 13% YoY growth. 
The conducive macroeconomic 
environment and improvement in overall 
economic activity were also evident in 
the improved sales of 3-wheelers and 
commercial vehicles, wherein retail 
sales grew by ~12%. At the same time, 
the auto OEM market continues to 
evolve. This is creating a gradual shift 
towards advanced lead-acid formats 
such as EFB, and AGM. In addition, 
as localisation of the EV supply chain 
gathers pace in India and OEM interest 
in domestic sourcing strengthens, 
the lithium-ion space is emerging 
as an important growth driver over

Auxiliary Battery for EVs
While electric vehicles are powered by lithium-ion batteries 
for propulsion, they continue to rely on lead-acid batteries 
for auxiliary functions, including dashboards, infotainment 
systems, lighting and power control units. This creates a 
parallel and recurring demand stream for reliable low-voltage 
energy storage solutions. 
As EV adoption accelerates, the installed base of vehicles 
requiring auxiliary batteries is expected to expand steadily. 
Exide, supported by its strong brand equity, extensive 
distribution network and proven product reliability, is well 
positioned to capitalise on this emerging opportunity.
Transition to Next-Gen Battery Technology
The transition towards more advanced battery technologies 
continues to gather pace. Automotive OEMs are increasingly 
adopting ISS and EFB batteries, along with Auxiliary batteries 
for electric vehicles, to comply with emission norms, improve 
fuel efficiency and meet evolving customer expectations. 
These products require specialised manufacturing capabilities, 
stringent quality controls and technical expertise, thereby 
increasing entry barriers. This structural shift presents a 
sustained opportunity for established manufacturers such as 
Exide.
Datacenter opportunity
India’s datacentre market is projected to grow approximately 
3–4 times by 2030, supported by lower land and construction 
costs and policy initiatives aimed at strengthening the country’s 
position as a global hub for digital infrastructure. These include 
tax holidays till 2047 for eligible foreign cloud service providers, 
adoption of advanced cooling technologies and the development 
of reliable power solutions by supporting future deployment of 
small modular and micro nuclear reactors under the SHANTI 
(Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for 
Transforming India) Act.

Risk Management
Amid an increasingly dynamic business environment, effective risk 
management plays an instrumental role in sustaining our consistent 
performance and delivering on our long-term commitments. We approach 
risk as a strategic consideration that informs decisions at every level of the 
organisation, rather than as a standalone function. 
Our Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework was refined during the year through the inclusion of 
insights from a formal Double Materiality Assessment (DMA). This ensures that sustainability-related risks and 
opportunities are systematically reflected in our risk register. 
Risk Management Framework 
Our ERM process
Our ERM framework draws upon 
globally recognised standards such 
as COSO and ISO 31000, while being 
thoughtfully adapted to align with the 
realities of our business and operating 
context. Risk management is woven 
into our annual business planning 
cycle, allowing it to inform decisions in a 
continuous and structured manner. 
The process brings together top-down 
inputs from leadership and bottom-
up inputs from business functions, 
providing us with a well-rounded 
understanding of risk across the 
organisation.
During the year, we introduced a Risk 
Intelligence Dashboard to support the 
near real-time monitoring of internal 
and external risk signals, including 
market trends, commodity movements, 
regulatory updates and industry 
developments.

Highlights of performance
Your Company reported net sales of H17,269 crore in 
FY 2025-26, as compared with H 16,588 crore in FY 2024-25, 
reflecting year-on-year growth of 4.1%. The performance was led 
by steady traction in the domestic business, with healthy growth 
in replacement business, Industrial-UPS and solar businesses. 
Domestic sales stood at H 16,326 crore, registering impressive 
growth over the previous year. Within this, Trade continued to 
deliver a strong performance with double digit growth, while the 
Institutional business also recorded impressive growth. On the 
other hand, international business remained under pressure 
during the year, with exports declining significantly year-on-year. 
This was on the backdrop of broader geopolitical dynamics 
including tariff challenges prevailed during the year.
Despite this mixed and challenging operating environment, 
the Company delivered stable profitability. Profit before 
depreciation, finance cost and tax (EBIDTA) stood at 
H 1,943 crore as against H 1,893 crore in the previous year, 
with EBIDTA margin at 11.3% in FY 2025-26. Profit before 
exceptional items and tax increased to H 1,500 crore from 
H 1,441 crore in FY 2024-25.
The year’s performance also reflects the strength of the 
Company’s balance sheet, with a strong cash position and a 
net debt zero status, providing requisite financial bandwidth to 
support growth initiatives while preserving resilience.

The details of the major domestic subsidiaries are given below:
Chloride Metals Limited
Chloride Metals Limited (CML), the wholly owned material 
subsidiary of Exide, is engaged in secondary lead smelting 
and refining including world class battery breaking process. 
CML has pan-India presence with manufacturing units in 
Karnataka, Maharashtra and West Bengal, equipped with 
advanced machinery and environmentally friendly production 
technologies. Its production capabilities are backed by 
robust design engineering cell and a rigorous quality control 
framework, furthering the circular economy model in the 
lead-acid battery industry and highlighting Exide’s focus of 
being a ‘responsible corporate citizen’.
During the year, the focus of CML was to optimise the utilisation 
of the capacities created in the previous year and improving 
overall productivity and process efficiency across operations. As 
a result, recycled lead production increased by approximately 
10% year‑on‑year, while recycled plastic production grew by 
around 5%, reflecting improved capacity utilisation and effective 
circular material usage.
CML delivered a steady performance in FY 2025-26, with 
revenue growing by ~5% year-on-year, while EBIDTA recording 
a significant improvement of 134% growth over the previous 
year. Sustained cost optimisation initiatives and operational 
efficiencies were the primary growth drivers behind the 
improved performance during the year under review.
Exide Energy Solutions Limited
Exide Energy Solutions Limited (EESL), the wholly owned 
material subsidiary of the Company was incorporated in the 
year 2022 with an objective to manufacture advanced chemistry 
battery cells for India’s electric mobility and stationary storage 
applications. Currently, it is manufacturing battery modules 
and packs for electric vehicles, telecom, and energy storage 
applications at its Prantij facility in Gujarat.
EESL is in advanced stage of commissioning a state‑of‑the‑art 
greenfield lithium‑ion cell manufacturing facility at the Hi‑Tech 
Defence & Aerospace Park (Phase‑II), Bengaluru. The project 
is being developed on an 80-acre site, with a planned capacity 
of 12 GWh in two phases of 6 GWh each. During the year 
under review, there was significant progress across installation, 
integration and commissioning activities spanning electrode 
manufacturing, cell assembly, and formation processes at the 
Bengaluru facility. Digital manufacturing and process monitoring 
systems have also been deployed to enable improve process 
stability, traceability, and operational efficiency at gigafactory 
scale. The cylindrical line, which is meant for 2-wheelers, is 
already under internal validation and customer sample supplies 
are expected to happen in next few months. The prismatic line 
is close to starting sample production, the commissioning of 
which is targeted in FY 2026-27.
Meanwhile, EESL continues to engage with various OEMs for 
2-wheeler, 3-wheeler, 4-wheeler and stationary energy providers 
across key end markets and initial commercial dispatches are 
expected to commence in FY 2026-27.

projects, Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) systems, within‑fence

Brief Outline on CSR Policy of the Company
	
Exide’s Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) philosophy is centred on creating meaningful, measurable, and sustainable 
impact aligned with India’s inclusive development priorities. The Company follows an integrated CSR approach that focuses 
on enabling secure and sustainable livelihoods, improving access to quality education, promoting environmental sustainability, 
and strengthening community well being.
	
The Company is committed to supporting underprivileged communities while strengthening the nation’s overall development 
framework. Its CSR initiatives are designed to align economic, environmental, and social goals with key national priorities such 
as access to quality education, climate action, skill development, livelihood generation, healthcare, sanitation, and inclusivity—
ultimately creating a meaningful and lasting positive impact on the lives of project participants.
	
With a strong commitment to building resilient and self-reliant communities, Exide implements strategic and innovative CSR 
programs aimed at fostering a sustainable future.
	
Exide’s CSR efforts are governed by a Board-approved policy guided by the vision of “Creating Shared Value for Sustainable 
Development of Communities.” These programs are aligned with the provisions of Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013, 
and are overseen by a Board-level committee.
	
The Company’s CSR approach emphasizes responsiveness, adaptability, and inclusivity in addressing the evolving needs and 
aspirations of nearby communities. Further details on Exide’s CSR policy are available on its official website.
	
The Company's CSR policy can be accessed on its website at https://www.exideindustries.com/sustainability/csr-policy.aspx.

The Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report (BRSR) 
is a framework developed by Securities and Exchange Board 
of India (SEBI) ensuring transparency and accountability in 
Environment, Social and Governance (ESG) reporting. It serves 
as a comprehensive framework for organizations’ to benchmark 
their sustainability efforts and demonstrate their commitment 
to responsible business conduct. In case of Exide, the BRSR 
report captures key ESG standards and initiatives undertaken 
by the Company. 
To enhance transparency and accountability, Exide is publishing 
the Business Responsibility Report (BRR) since the financial 
year (FY) 2014-15. Starting from FY 2021-22, the Company 
has further strengthened its reporting by including detailed 
ESG initiatives within the BRSR framework. This reporting 
framework enables Exide to provide stakeholders with a more 
comprehensive understanding of our ESG efforts, performance, 
and future targets. Through this, Exide aims to provide greater 
transparency, engage stakeholders, and drive positive change 
beyond financials diversifying towards environmental and 
social impacts. 
‘Embracing sustainability is not just a corporate vision, but 
a regular aspect of our culture and business operations. It 
is ingrained in our business strategy and is central to the 
trust placed in our Company by customers, employees 
and partners alike. We endeavor to create economic 
value and make a positive impact in every market 
through resource conservation, safety enhancement and 
philanthropic investments’.

At Exide Industries Limited, sustainability is not a parallel initiative but a foundational 
element of our operating model. Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) 
considerations are embedded across strategy, risk management and execution 
to ensure long-term value creation for stakeholders and communities. During 
FY 2025-26, the Company navigated key sustainability risks, including carbon 
emission intensity, water and waste management challenges, raw material price 
volatility, value chain emissions exposure and an evolving regulatory landscape, 
while continuing to advance clearly defined sustainability targets.
Sustainability risks and performance are overseen through strong governance 
mechanisms, with regular review by the Senior Leadership Team and the Risk 
Management Committee. Our Enterprise Risk Management framework, aligned 
with COSO principles and ISO 31000, is designed to safeguard the interests of 
all stakeholders by addressing a wide spectrum of risks — including strategic, 
reputational, ESG, compliance, operational and financial exposures. We 
continuously strengthen our procedures, systems and internal controls so that 
this framework remains responsive to the evolving risk environment and firmly 
integrated with our sustainability vision and business plan. A core mitigation 
lever is our circular economy model, under which nearly 79% of lead and lead 
alloys are sourced from recycled materials, a majority being contributed through 
our wholly-owned subsidiary, Chloride Metals Limited. This closed-loop recovery 
and reintegration system enhances resource security, mitigates cost volatility 
and ensures compliance with Extended Producer Responsibility obligations 
under the Battery Waste Management Rules, E-waste Rules and Plastic Waste 
Management Rules, reflecting a shift from compliance-led actions to genuine 
circularity. In addition, we incorporate approximately nearly 16% recycled plastic 
in our operations, further reinforcing our commitment to sustainable resource use.
De carbonisation and resource efficiency remain central to sustainability risk 
mitigation. Renewable energy accounted for 24%+ of our electricity mix during 
the year, supported by process improvements, energy efficiency measures and 
ongoing solar and wind capacity additions. Water-related risks are addressed 
through water stewardship projects, Zero Liquid Discharge systems, within-fence 
rainwater collection and community-based outside-fence interventions, collectively 
advancing our ambition towards water neutrality. In logistics, electric vehicles in 
the 0-50 km last-mile segment now represent 26% of monthly delivery volumes, 
exceeding our 2030 target and reducing Scope 3 emissions exposure.
Sustainable innovation further strengthens resilience, with continuous R&D 
enabling the expansion of environmentally responsible and next-generation 
products. Independent validation enhances transparency and stakeholder 
confidence, as reflected in our S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment 
score of 65, placing Exide in the top 5 percentile globally in the Auto Components 
sector and earning recognition as a Sustainability Yearbook Member and Industry 
Mover. Our EcoVadis sustainability rating, assessed across Environment, Labour & 
Human Rights, Ethics and Sustainable Procurement, improved, helping us secure 
a Bronze Medal placing in the 75th percentile.

in FY 2024–25 through Phase 1 of its Supplier ESG programme, covering awareness, assessments, and ESG data 
reviews. In FY 2025–26, Phase 2 initiatives have focused on sustainable procurement integration and targeted supplier

To enhance vendor management and drive digitalisation, Exide is expanding the adoption of e-sourcing through the SAP

b.	
If yes, what percentage of inputs were sourced sustainably?
	
	
Recognising lead as the most critical raw material in battery manufacturing, Exide is strongly committed to circular and 
sustainable sourcing. Recycled lead and lead alloy utilisation increased to nearly 79% in FY 2025-26, underscoring the 
Company's commitment to the circular economy and significantly reducing dependence on virgin material extraction.
	
	
Exide sources a substantial portion of its recycled lead requirements through Chloride Metals Limited (CML), its 
wholly-owned subsidiary engaged in secondary lead smelting and refining, with manufacturing facilities in Karnataka, 
Maharashtra, and West Bengal. CML's recycling infrastructure has been steadily strengthened — with smelting units 
commissioned at Haldia (FY 2021-22) and SUPA, Ahmednagar (FY 2023-24) augmenting the existing facility at Malur. 
Recycled lead production increased by approximately 10% year-on-year in FY 2025-26, reflecting improved capacity 
utilisation and sustained operational focus. Looking ahead, a significant capacity addition at the Haldia plant is expected 
to be commissioned by Q4 FY 2026-27. This is projected to increase overall lead recycling capacity by approximately 
30%, further strengthening the circular sourcing model.
	
	
Recycled plastic utilisation in battery manufacturing was maintained at approximately 16% in FY 2025-26, with recycled 
plastic production growing by approximately 5% year-on-year. Sustainable sourcing of recycled plastics remains a 
continuing area of focus.
	
	
Exide's sourcing policies prioritise a continuous increase in sustainable procurement. Our comprehensive process, 
covering vendor selection to post-contract support, incorporates stepwise evaluation criteria including periodic supplier 
audits of Tier 1 and Tier 2 suppliers. We have also started assessing ISO 14001 and 45001 certifications, ESG commitments, 
and supplier roles for our top suppliers. As a key onboarding step, suppliers are required to accept our updated Supplier 
Code of Conduct, Sustainable Sourcing & Procurement Policy, and Vendor Manual as part of entering RFPs. This ensures 
supplier alignment with our sustainability objectives and responsible practices throughout the supply chain.
	
	
Regular engagement with vendors and service providers supports transparency, collaboration and continuous improvement.

Describe the processes in place to safely reclaim your products for reusing, recycling and disposing at the end of 
life, for (a) Plastics (including packaging) (b) E-waste (c) Hazardous waste and (d) other wastes.
	
(a)	 Battery Waste
	
	
Exide is registered under the Battery Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2023 as a Producer and is committed to 
meeting prescribed recycling targets.
	
	
End-of-life batteries are collected through a pan India network spanning dealers, institutional customers, and OEMs, 
managed through pricing mechanisms, buyback schemes, contract clauses, and auction arrangements. Used batteries 
are transported through a reverse logistics process to designated smelting units for safe lead recovery. Battery recycling 
is conducted through the Company's backward integration model, with facilities in Karnataka, Maharashtra, and West 
Bengal. Recycled lead is consumed directly in battery production, closing the material loop.

Consumer awareness is built through warranty cards and packaging directing customers to designated collection 
centres. A multi-channel awareness programme reinforces collection, reaching end consumers through community 
seminars, engaging dealers through dedicated meets on collection responsibilities, and training internal functions across 
Sales, Procurement, EHS, Legal, and Risk Management on EPR compliance. EPR certificates are tracked and transferred 
digitally through the CPCB portal. 
	
(b)	 Plastics
	
	
Exide is registered under the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016. An authorised vendor partnership enables 
collection and recycling of plastic packaging waste, with credits transferred to Exide in accordance with CPCB norms. 
Recycled plastic utilisation on the other hand for battery manufacturing stands at approximately 16%, with further increase 
a continuing focus. 
	
(c)	 E-Waste
	
	
Under the E-Waste Management Rules, 2023, Exide is registered as a Producer for inverters and UPS systems and has 
initiated compliance steps including engagement with authorised e-waste recyclers and establishment of end-of-life 
collection mechanisms. 
	
(d)	 Other Waste
	
	
ETP sludge from Hosur is channelled to cement and other industries following Pollution Control Board approvals. Similar 
approvals are being pursued for remaining facilities.

Whether an occupational health and safety management system has been implemented by the entity? (Yes /

sites, certified to ISO 45001 and managed by dedicated EHS teams. Safety performance and risk mitigation are reviewed 
periodically by senior management and at ESG governance forums, supported by regular internal and external audits by 
certified bodies.
	
	
The OHS management system covers permanent employees, contractual workforce, service providers, and visitors 
operating within the Company's premises. Key safety performance indicators, including Total Recordable Injury Rate 
(TRIR), Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate (LTIFR), near-miss reporting, and Unsafe Act/Unsafe Condition (UA-UC) 
observations — are monitored through monthly EHS reviews across locations to strengthen incident reporting, corrective 
action tracking, and proactive risk identification
	
	
Governance & Safety Committees
	
	
Safety Committees have been established across all factories with statutory representation from employees and workers. 
These committees monitor implementation of safety protocols, review employee health status and risk exposure, 
recommend workplace improvements, and promote participative safety culture through hazard identification and 
behavioural safety initiatives.
	
	
Training & Awareness Programs
	
	
Safety preparedness is built through induction training and mock drills for all new employees including contractual workers. 
	
	
Employees are trained in first aid, emergency response, and near-miss identification and reporting. 
	
	
Those working in high-risk areas receive specialised risk-based training to address specific occupational hazards. 
	
	
Each process is assigned a Safety Champion to promote a strong safety culture and encourage employee participation 
in risk mitigation. 
	
	
Regular toolbox talks, safety campaigns, and behavioural safety programmes reinforce a proactive safety culture 
across operations.
	
	
Occupational Health Centers & Emergency Medical Support
	
	
Occupational Health Centres are operational across all sites, staffed with qualified medical doctors and nursing 
professionals. These centres provide prompt medical assistance for health incidents and workplace injuries, and 
support occupational health surveillance, periodic medical examinations, preventive health monitoring, and employee 
wellness initiatives.
	
	
Contractor Safety Management
	
	
Structured contractor safety management is in place, covering safety induction, competency verification, work permit 
systems, and supervision mechanisms to ensure safe execution of contracted activities.
	
	
EHS Policy Commitment
	
	
Exide's EHS Policy reflects the Company's commitment to continuous improvement in occupational health and safety 
standards, strict adherence to legal and statutory requirements, and fostering a culture of safety awareness among all 
stakeholders — aligned with global ESG frameworks and responsible workplace practices.

b.	
What are the processes used to identify work related hazards and assess risks on a routine and non-routine 
basis by the entity?
	
	
Routine Activities - Hazard Identification & Risk Assessment (HIRA) Framework
	
	
Exide follows a structured Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) framework across all operations to 
systematically identify, evaluate, and mitigate workplace hazards associated with routine activities. The framework 
scans each process and operational activity to identify potential hazards, their causes, possible consequences, and 
risk exposure. Existing control measures are evaluated and strengthened through a hierarchy of controls, engineering 
controls, administrative controls, and PPE based on risk prioritisation.
	
	
Proactive hazard detection is supported through Unsafe Act / Unsafe Condition (UA-UC) reporting, behavioural safety 
observations, workplace safety inspections, and near-miss reporting. Continuous improvement is embedded through 
Kaizen initiatives, encouraging employee-led safety improvements across operations.
	
	
Non-Routine Activities - Permit-to-Work System
	
	
For non-routine and high-risk activities, detailed task-specific risk assessments are conducted prior to execution, 
evaluating hazard severity, likelihood, and environmental conditions. These activities are governed through a structured 
Permit-to-Work (PTW) system, which ensures implementation of specialised safety controls, formal safety clearances, 
and verification of worker competency and supervision before commencement.
	
	
The PTW system covers high-risk activities including confined space entry, hot work, work at height, electrical isolation, 
and maintenance interventions.
	
	
Periodic Review & Update
	
	
Risk assessments are periodically reviewed and updated based on operational changes, incident learnings, safety 
audits, and regulatory developments — ensuring safety controls remain current and effective.

Yes. Exide has established structured mechanisms for employees to report work-related hazards and remove themselves

Stop Work Authority
	
	
Employees are explicitly empowered to stop work or remove themselves from a task if they perceive an unsafe condition

Employee Participation

strengthening collective responsibility for workplace safety.

Measures for a Safe and Healthy Workplace
	
Exide has implemented a structured framework for workplace safety and health management across all manufacturing facilities, 
certified to ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 by TUV-NORD. The EHS Policy, established by senior management and displayed across 
all operational locations, sets the foundation for compliance with statutory requirements and international best practices.
	
Governance & Safety Culture
	
Safety Committees are functional across all factories and offices, with statutory representation from employees and workers, 
overseeing safety compliance and driving employee participation. The Safety Champions Programme deploys trained 
employees at each process to proactively identify and report unsafe conditions. Regular toolbox talks, behavioural safety 
programmes, and awareness campaigns reinforce a culture of shared responsibility across the workforce.
	
Hazard Identification & Risk Management
	
Cross-functional EHS teams at each facility are responsible for hazard identification, risk assessment, and compliance 
enforcement. Risk assessments are conducted through the HIRA framework for routine activities and through a Permit-
to-Work system for non-routine and high-risk tasks. Learnings from incidents, near-misses, and safety observations are 
systematically analysed to strengthen preventive controls.
	
Safety Infrastructure
	
Physical and digital safety infrastructure is maintained across all facilities, covering:
 
 
Emergency Preparedness: Fire alarms, extinguishers, hydrants, emergency exits, signage, and designated assembly 
areas; periodic mock drills and emergency response training ensure operational readiness
 
 
Occupational Health Facilities: On-site medical rooms, first-aid stations, OHC facilities staffed with qualified medical 
and nursing professionals, clean drinking water, sanitation, and ergonomic setups
 
 
Machine Safety: Machine guarding, interlocks, ventilation, and fume extraction systems
 
 
Hazardous Material Management: Designated storage areas, spill control kits, MSDS availability, and waste 
handling systems
 
 
Digital Safety Systems: CCTV, access control, gas detectors, and digital permit-to-work and monitoring tools
 
 
Training Infrastructure: Dedicated safety training rooms, DOJO-based experiential learning areas, drill practice zones, 
and communication boards
 
 
PPE Management: Adequate provision, storage, and maintenance systems for essential PPE across all roles 
and risk levels
	
Training & Continuous Improvement
	
All employees and workers undergo structured safety induction and skill-based training from day one. The training framework 
spans multiple formats: internal trainer-led sessions, hybrid classroom and digital modules, refresher training programmes, 
and a dedicated Office Health & Safety training module ensuring coverage beyond the shop floor to office-based employees. 
DOJO-based experiential learning areas provide hands-on hazard familiarisation and practical safety skill-building.
	
In FY 2025-26, Exide recorded nearly 1,98,000 Health & Safety related training hours across the organisation, reflecting the 
scale and depth of safety capability building embedded across all locations and employee categories.
	
Internal audits by corporate EHS teams are complemented by periodic external audits to ensure independent assessment 
and continuous improvement. Near-miss reporting, safety observations, and incident investigations feed into a systematic 
corrective and preventive action cycle, ensuring ongoing strengthening of safety controls across operations.

Corrective Actions for Safety-Related Incidents and Risk Mitigation
	
All workplace incidents and near-miss events are subject to structured root cause analysis (RCA) to identify underlying causes 
and determine appropriate corrective and preventive actions. Findings are documented and tracked through a digital CAPA 
system, with open actions reviewed at plant-level safety committee meetings and escalated to senior management where 
necessary. Notifiable incidents are reported to factory inspectorates and other applicable regulatory bodies in accordance with 
statutory requirements.
	
Corrective Action Process
	
Incidents are investigated by cross-functional EHS teams, with root cause findings used to strengthen engineering controls, 
revise standard operating procedures, and update training content where required. The effectiveness of implemented controls 
is monitored through monthly EHS reviews, ensuring sustained improvement and timely closure of open actions.
	
Proactive Risk Mitigation Measures
	
Beyond incident response, the following preventive measures are in place to reduce risk exposure:
 
 
Medical surveillance and health check-ups- periodic monitoring for employees in high-risk roles, with early intervention 
where health risks are identified
 
 
Job rotation- structured rotation to reduce repetitive stress and prolonged hazardous exposure
 
 
Engineering controls- ongoing investment in machine guarding, ventilation, fume extraction, and process modification to 
eliminate or reduce hazards at source
 
 
Safety training- refresher training, hybrid sessions, and role-specific modules ensure current and relevant hazard 
awareness across the workforce
 
 
Reward and recognition- structured schemes acknowledge safe behaviour and near-miss reporting, reinforcing a 
proactive safety culture and encouraging employee participation in risk identification

Principle 6: 
Exide is committed to reducing its environmental footprint across energy, materials, water, and logistics, embedding resource 
efficiency and circularity into both operations and product development.
Energy & Emissions: Renewable energy constitutes 24%+ of the electricity mix, with solar capacities commissioned in FY 2025-26 
and a target of 30% by 2030. Energy efficiency measures have delivered year-on-year reductions in both grid electricity and non-
renewable fuel consumption. Scope 1 and 2 emissions undergo Reasonable Assurance under BRSR Core requirements; Scope 3 
across 10 categories undergoes Limited Assurance, providing a fully assured GHG disclosure framework.
Materials & Circularity: Nearly 79% recycled lead and lead alloys and nearly 16% recycled plastics are used in production, 
supported by the backward integration model for end-of-life battery processing and lead recovery. Life Cycle Assessments have 
been conducted for three battery products in accordance with ISO 14040 guidelines.
Water: Water management spans operational efficiency and watershed stewardship. The 3R strategy is supported by RO plants, 
ZLD systems at two factories and process in one. Site-specific process transitions at Ahmednagar yielded approximately 15% 
freshwater savings. In FY 25-26, while water consumption has increased with production growth, improving water efficiency 
remains a priority. Through a combined within-fence and outside-fence interventions, within the same and adjacent watersheds/
aquifers an annual water conservation and recharge potential of 6,00,000 KL+ was created during the year, supporting the pathway 
toward Water Neutrality.
Logistics: LNG trucks have been introduced for primary freight at select locations and 26% of last-mile (0-50km) deliveries are 
handled by electric vehicles.
Exide's environmental performance was independently validated through the EcoVadis assessment, where we secured an EcoVadis 
Bronze Medal. At S&P Corporate Sustainability Assessment, we scored 65/100, top 5 percentile in Auto Components

10.	 Briefly describe the waste management practices adopted in your establishments. Describe the strategy adopted 
by your company to reduce usage of hazardous and toxic chemicals in your products and processes and the 
practices adopted to manage such wastes
	
Waste Management Practices & Hazardous Chemical Reduction
	
Exide manages waste across all manufacturing facilities in accordance with applicable regulations, including the Hazardous 
Waste Management Rules, Factories Act, and Environmental Protection Act etc. This is consistent with ISO 14001 certified 
environmental management systems.
	
Waste Segregation & Resource Recovery
	
All manufacturing locations have implemented structured, colour-coded waste segregation systems focused on recycling, 
resource recovery, and responsible disposal through authorised channels. Four facilities use advanced waste segregation 
supported by digital tracking and real-time monitoring, ensuring full traceability and regulatory compliance across hazardous 
and non-hazardous waste streams.
	
Notable outcomes in FY 2025-26 include recycling of over 3,700 MT+ of lead waste at Shyamnagar; production of 600 
plastic crates from recycled scrap at Taloja; and implementation of reverse logistics for packaging waste at Haridwar 
and Roorkee — reinforcing circular economy principles across the manufacturing network.
	
Lead waste is tracked through certified recycling units, with strengthened partnerships with government-certified hazardous 
waste management contractors for compliant processing. Recycled lead from end-of-life batteries processed through the 
backward integration model and other material sourcing strategies, currently stood at nearly 79% of total lead consumption. 
This directly reduces virgin material dependency and associated waste generation.
	
Co-Processing & Zero-Waste Disposal
	
ETP sludge and PE separators from three factories are co-processed in cement manufacturing as alternative fuels and raw 
materials, minimising landfill dependency. Predictive analytics are used to optimise chemical usage in effluent treatment, 
reducing sludge generation. Four of our sites are self-assessed to be Zero-waste to Landfill, which has been verified through 
external assurance. 
	
Single-Use Plastic Reduction
	
Reusable battery storage bins have been introduced to reduce single-use plastics in storage and handling. Advanced material 
substitution has been implemented at select facilities to eliminate single-use plastics in packaging and logistics. EPR traceability 
through authorised plastic recycler partnerships supports closed-loop plastic waste management.
	
Hazardous & Toxic Chemical Reduction Strategy
	
Exide's approach to reducing hazardous and toxic chemical usage operates at both product and process levels. At the 
product level, the use of nearly 79% recycled lead reduces the need for primary lead smelting, a process associated 
with significantly higher hazardous emissions and waste generation. At the process level, product design and process re-
engineering initiatives are undertaken on an ongoing basis to progressively reduce the use of hazardous and toxic chemicals in 
manufacturing. Hazardous materials are managed through designated storage areas, spill control systems, and Material Safety 
Data Sheets (MSDS) — with all employees trained on safe handling procedures. At organisational level ROHS certification is 
also undertaken.

Does the entity have a business continuity and disaster management plan? Give details in 100 words/ web link.
	
Yes. Exide maintains a structured Business Continuity Plan (BCP) across all operations, covering physical, operational, and 
digital risk scenarios.
	
Physical & Operational Resilience: Emergency preparedness infrastructure, including fire alarms, extinguishers, hydrants, 
emergency exits, signage, and assembly areas etc. maintained across all facilities. The BCP covers emergency declaration 
procedures, evacuation plans, safe plant shutdown protocols, and incident-specific action plans. Employees are trained on 
roles and responsibilities, signalling mechanisms, assembly points, medical arrangements, and Material Safety Data Sheets 
(MSDS) for hazardous materials. Risk assessments are conducted for critical business activities with proactive mitigation plans 
maintained for adverse conditions.
	
IT & Cyber Resilience: A formal Information Technology Risk Management (ITRM) framework governs systematic 
identification, assessment, mitigation, and monitoring of IT-related risks. An IT Risk Register tracks identified risks with 
likelihood and impact ratings, assigned owners, and defined mitigation timelines. Regular Vulnerability Assessments and 
Penetration Testing (VAPT), IT General Controls (ITGC) reviews covering logical access, change management, backup 
and disaster recovery, and security gap assessments against ISO 27001 and applicable regulatory standards are conducted 
periodically. A Cybersecurity and IT Disaster Recovery Plan is maintained as part of the broader BCP framework.
	
HR Data & Process Security: A centralised, access-controlled HRIS manages employee data with automated onboarding, 
role change, and separation workflows. Integration with enterprise Identity and Access Management (IAM) platforms 
ensures role-based access controls and segregation of duties. Digital onboarding and periodic training modules are delivered 
through an integrated Learning Management System (LMS).

downtime. BCP frameworks are periodically reviewed and updated to reflect evolving operational and cyber risk

Describe the mechanisms to receive and redress grievances of the community
	
Exide prioritizes continuous engagement with local panchayats and communities to understand and proactively address their 
aspirations and concerns, extending beyond operational impact to encompass their overall well-being. Tailored CSR initiatives 
directly reflects this commitment.

At all Exide facilities, systematic consultation processes gather valuable suggestions, feedback, and grievances. Our robust 
grievance redressal mechanism ensures prompt local resolution by plant-level CSR sub-committees, with a clear escalation 
pathway for unresolved issues. Recognizing local communities as vital stakeholders, these sub-committees actively collaborate 
with local bodies and organizations to identify needs and co-create impactful CSR projects. Throughout the project lifecycle, 
from design to handover, active stakeholder engagement and independent third-party assessments, alongside central CSR 
team monitoring, ensure accountability and responsiveness. This comprehensive approach underscores Exide's dedication to 
community welfare and long-term sustainable relationships.
	
Additionally, the stakeholders can also raise their concerns directly with CSR department through a dedicated e-mail id: 
csr@exide.co.in.
	
Exide has implemented a QR code–based feedback mechanism to streamline grievance redressal and ensure timely 
stakeholder engagement. This system allows community members, project participants, and other stakeholders to provide 
feedback, suggestions, or register complaints directly through a simple scan of a QR code using their smartphones. Once 
scanned, users are directed to a simple digital form where they can submit their concerns, which are automatically logged in 
Exide’s CSR management system. The participant may log their concern while being anonymous. 
	
The mechanism offers several advantages:
 
 
Accessibility: Feedback can be provided anytime and anywhere, eliminating barriers of distance or limited access to 
plant offices. 
 
 
Transparency and Accountability: Each grievance is mapped directly to Head of CSR, ensuring that stakeholders can 
receive timely updates on the status of their concerns. The grievances are reviewed once every 15 days.
 
 
Data-driven insights: The digital system allows Exide to analyse recurring issues, identify trends, and improve project 
planning and execution based on real-time feedback. 
	
By leveraging this QR code–enabled system, Exide strengthens its commitment to being a responsive and responsible 
partner, ensuring that the voices of vulnerable and marginalized stakeholders are heard and addressed efficiently.

Describe the mechanisms in place to receive and respond to consumer complaints and feedback
	
Exide operates a structured, multi-channel complaint resolution system across automotive, home UPS, OEM, and 
institutional segments.
	
B2C (Replacement segment)
	
A two-tier service model underpins B2C delivery: Service 1.0 empowers dealers with diagnostic tools and streamlined 
warranty processes; Service 2.0 provides customers direct access via WhatsApp, toll-free numbers, and online platforms with 
doorstep assistance in major cities. Over 1,600+ Exide Care outlets across India serve as primary customer touchpoints for 
service, warranty, and product support, complemented by seamless digital warranty registration.
	
Specialised offerings include Exide Batmobile for automotive battery doorstep service and Exide Home Service for inverter and 
UPS maintenance. Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMC) provide structured preventive maintenance, reducing service downtime. 
The Exide Samrat loyalty programme builds a trained, brand-aligned mechanic community supporting last-mile service delivery.
	
B2B (OEM & Institutional)
	
The Exide EDGE CRM platform (Salesforce FSL) manages service calls end-to-end, with real-time technician tracking, 
digital diagnostics, automated warranty determination, and OTP-based validation. Customers connect via toll-free numbers 
and QR code scanning. The Dealer Management System (DMS) enables real-time service updates and faster warranty 
processing for channel partners. Specialist service personnel are deployed nationwide for proactive OEM and institutional 
account management. Sector-focused engagement covers Healthcare, BFSI, and IT/ITes segments, with GeM presence and 
Rate Contracts establishing Exide as preferred supplier in government procurement.
	
Dealer & Ecosystem Capability
	
Dealer training and technician certification programmes cover battery diagnostics, warranty evaluation, and BS VI vehicle 
service readiness. Digital dealer infrastructure audits ensure consistent service standards across markets. In FY 2025-26, 
52 youths were enrolled under the Exide Samrat programme and 275 youths trained under RPL mode for the automobile 
trade, strengthening technical competency across the service ecosystem.
	
All complaints are investigated through root cause analysis, with remedial actions tracked for continuous improvement.

Steps taken to inform and educate consumers about safe and responsible usage of products and/or services. 
	
Exide provides safety and responsible usage information through multiple channels across the product lifecycle.
	
Product packaging includes details on product description, composition, safe handling and usage instructions, warranty 
terms, dealer service guidance, and end-of-life disposal information, including mandatory EPR numbers for battery tracking 
and responsible disposal under applicable waste management regulations. Digital warranty registration, with 60 lakh+ 
registrations - reinforces consumer onboarding, product traceability, and post-purchase engagement.
	
Channel partners are regularly trained on product features, safety requirements, and responsible usage through structured 
dealer programmes, technician certification initiatives, and product catalogues. Awareness on safe battery disposal and EPR 
obligations is built through dedicated programmes covering dealers, institutional customers, and end consumers — including 
community outreach sessions targeting school teachers, students, and underprivileged youth on waste management and 
sustainable practices.
	
Consumers can access product safety and usage information through the Company's websites, electronic media, and customer 
support channels including toll-free numbers and WhatsApp. Sales and customer support teams proactively communicate 
safety and usage guidance to institutional and retail customers on an ongoing basis.

Exide supplies critical sectors including Railways, Telecom, Defence, and the Indian Navy, sectors where supply continuity is of

in these segments, providing advance notice of any significant supply-related developments, product transitions, or operational 
changes that may affect service continuity.
	
Information is shared through direct communication, email notifications, and website updates, ensuring transparency and 
proactive engagement with essential service customers. Where required, contingency planning and inventory management 
measures are coordinated with customers to minimise disruption risk.

 GOVERNANCE PHILOSOPHY
Corporate Governance is an integral and internalized process 
that guides Exide Industries Limited (“Exide/Company”) in 
its pursuit of sustainable value creation for all stakeholders, 
including shareholders, customers, employees, and the society 
in which it operates. The Company firmly believes that while 
large corporates utilize significant societal and economic 
resources to generate wealth and create value, it is sound 
corporate governance that ensures such value creation is 
sustainable, responsible, and enduring.
Corporate Governance at Exide extends beyond mere 
adherence 
to 
prescribed 
processes 
and 
statutory 
compliances. It reflects the role the Company envisions for 
itself for today, tomorrow, and in the long term, anchored in 
ethical conduct, accountability, and responsible decision-
making. The governance framework is driven by a clear “tone 
at the top”, a robust and effective Board and Committee 
structure, and strong management systems supported by 
well-defined internal controls, a comprehensive code of 
conduct, an effective risk management framework, and a suite 
of policies and procedures.
In its commitment to fostering an ethical corporate culture and 
responsible corporate citizenship, the Company’s governance 
philosophy 
rests 
on 
certain 
core 
tenets—trusteeship, 
transparency, empowerment and accountability, control, and 
ethical corporate citizenship.
The Company believes that by embedding and integrating these 
interconnected tenets into its operations and decision-making 
processes, an appropriate corporate culture is created—one 
that ensures the Company is managed in a manner consistent 
with the highest standards of ethical corporate citizenship. 
These principles are reinforced through mandatory ethics and 
compliance training programs for all employees, as well as 
through a confidential and effective whistleblower mechanism.
The tenet of trusteeship underscores the fiduciary responsibility 
of the Board of Directors to protect and enhance shareholder 
value while ensuring that the Company fulfils its obligations to all 
stakeholders. This responsibility is exercised through effective 
oversight of strategic direction, risk management, financial 
performance, and governance processes. Under this tenet, 
the Company also discharges its responsibilities in the broader 
economic and social spheres, thereby enabling sustainable 
and responsible growth.
The Company not only complies with the corporate 
governance requirements prescribed under the Securities and 
Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing Regulations”), 
but also strives to be among the best-governed companies. It 
remains committed to continuously strengthening and refining 
its governance practices in line with evolving stakeholder 
expectations, regulatory developments, and the dynamic 
business environment.

(2) (b) to (i) and Schedule V to the SEBI Listing Regulations, the 
report containing the details of Corporate Governance of Exide

At the apex of this governance framework is the Board of 
Directors, which provides strategic supervision on behalf of the 
shareholders. The Board comprises of Independent Directors 
with diverse competencies and experience across areas such 
as finance, technology, business strategy, and governance. 
The Board reviews and approves strategic plans, monitors 
organizational performance against defined objectives, and 
ensures alignment with the Company’s long-term vision 
and goals. While the Board remains distinct from day-to-day 
strategic management, it plays a pivotal role in guiding executive 
leadership with independence and objectivity, thereby ensuring 
accountability at all levels.
In addition, the Board is responsible for formulating key policies 
and governance frameworks, overseeing the Company’s 
risk management and internal control systems, and ensuring 
compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and ethical 
standards. The Board is supported in its oversight function 
by various Committees, including the Audit Committee, 
Nomination and Remuneration Committee, Stakeholders 
Relationship Committee and Risk Management Committee, 
which provide focused and specialized supervision in their 
respective domains.
At the operational level, the executive management of individual 
business divisions is focused on enhancing the quality, 
efficiency, and effectiveness of each business vertical. This 
level functions under the strategic and operational guidance 
of the Executive Committee (“ExCom”), which is entrusted with 
the overall vision and direction of the organization, including 
strategic growth, innovation, and stakeholder value creation. The 
ExCom comprises Senior Management Personnel from various 
functions and is led by the Managing Director & Chief Executive 
Officer. It acts as a critical enabler in implementing the strategic 
decisions approved by the Board, while also overseeing the 
day-to-day management of the Company’s affairs.
The effectiveness of this three-tier governance framework is 
underpinned by a clearly defined organizational structure, which 
delineates the roles, responsibilities, and authority vested in 
each governance layer. Each entity within the framework is 
appropriately empowered with the requisite authority to discharge 
its responsibilities effectively, ensuring seamless decision-
making, accountability, and sustained organizational growth.
